title: Record the Y-exit rank-lift loss against the centre budget
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Negative result. No new κ. The selected conditional value stays `781451/250000000`.

On the pinned round-three centre word, every Y exit chart has dimension 8 and sits strictly inside the unique dimension-9 frame. Raising all 112 of those charts to that frame and lowering them back is a legal pair of width-1 transports per exit, so it adds 224 rank-1 children and restores every exit chart. The emitted invoice has exactly eight width-8 transports, one per centre role, with rank mass 64. For every exponent `θ` in `(0, 1]`, deleting any submultiset of those transports saves at most that rank mass, because `r^θ ≤ r`. The paid moment therefore rises by at least 160. Deleting all eight attains 160 at `θ = 1`.

A one-way raise, without the return, still leaves a gap of at least 48 and does not restore the rank-8 exits. Helper targets stay at the retained histogram. This is not a caller, a selected-word decoder, or a search of the binary coframe class.

## Task and overlap

Base commit `7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a` on canonical `CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds` main. Priority revision 8. Catalogue card `complex-rank-shape-decoder`. Scope status: **changed**. Head `4b9581bc3805c67496d5dae250261b3e91001d94` on `unpaidmoon/integer-mult-bounds`, branch `cursor/y-exit-rank-lift-obstruction-b140`.

Session r106 takes item 9 of the ordered eligible list. Structured handoffs on discussion #1166 were read through comment 19464867 (`2026-11-07T22:19:22Z`). The 19 October index is closed. Later handoffs whose canonical artifact is an open pull request are excluded, including the 2 November review artifacts #6355, #6357, #6359, #6360, #6361, #6376, #6378 and #6396, and the later #6321 verification-caller updates through #6873. Work already delivered by this account, including the four-contact trees and the four-cycle certificate, is excluded. No unexpired structured claim covers this route. The revision-8 "Next bounded decisions" table then supplies six rows, and catalogue cards not named there follow:

1. Complex helpers (`p104-side-correction`, `coverage-law-change`).
2. BIT (`bit-helper-contract`).
3. New decoders and interfaces.
4. Supplier audit (`supplier-boundary-audit`).
5. All-size audit (`uniform-transfer-audit`).
6. Verification tooling (`replay-runtime`).
7. `bit-new-register-model`.
8. `r437-carrier-integration`.
9. **This package.** `complex-rank-shape-decoder`.
10. `complex-new-helper-inventory`.

Inside that card, #6289 prices independent chart pairs, #6306 prices induced three-contact paths, #6336 prices induced four-vertex trees, and open #6514 prices the induced four-cycles. The family note on #6514 treats a five-contact extension as a stop. The remaining named piece is the routing half of discussion #1166 comment 19133861: the 224-against-64 Y-exit lift, which that handoff states and does not check. This package is that check. It is distinct from #6516, which is a G20 frame round trip on a different word.

PR #5698 closes the compatible binary coframe class and is not this alphabet. The centre-chain terminal prices 112 rank-8 children and 114 rank-9 children, not 224 rank-1 children. Open PR titles on 2026-11-08 do not state this gap. No matches is not proof that a hidden diff is absent.

## Validation

CPython 3.12.3, standard library only. From the repository root:

```sh
python3 -B research/y-exit-rank-lift-obstruction/verify.py
python3 -O -B research/y-exit-rank-lift-obstruction/verify.py
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/y-exit-rank-lift-obstruction
python3 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/y-exit-rank-lift-obstruction --check-source-history
python3 -B scripts/research_selected_baseline.py
```

Observed `PASS_Y_EXIT_RANK_LIFT_OBSTRUCTION` with `round_trip_h1=224`, `rank_mass=64`, `moment_gap_at_least=160`, the same marker under `-O`, `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE` with outcome `negative-result`, `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES` at `4b9581bc3805c67496d5dae250261b3e91001d94`, and `PASS_RESEARCH_BASELINE_BINDINGS_ONLY`.

Controls reject a ninth centre call, a nonpositive deleted rank, a negative child count, and a width-2 claim for dimensions 8 and 9. Failures are exceptions, so `-O` does not disable them.

Not run: a physical caller, native phase beyond this emitter, Lean, Docker, and `make frontier6030-verify`.

## Credit

The word is Cao Yifan / intqwq, PR #4610. The width law and the eight-centre emitter are the retained centre extension in the contact-frontier package, following Cinna Davis and Dugongue's chart convention. Discussion #1166 comment 19133861, Chris R / Clear1nsight, named the 224-against-64 stop. The centre-chain terminal is a different bill. The one-transvection contact certificates are a different alphabet.

Prepared by unpaidmoon with substantial Cursor Grok assistance. Apache-2.0. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

## Open next questions

Recorded in `research/y-exit-rank-lift-obstruction/TASK.json` and the package README.

1. Can a route that moves only some Y exits, or that also deletes helper calls, clear a positive paid moment while restoring every rank-8 Y exit? First step: one literal route whose added rank mass is at most 64, with these exit charts and the 408 helper targets fixed. No such route is supplied here.
2. Can the one-way move onto frame 1 be accepted as an endpoint? It leaves a gap of at least 48 and replaces each rank-8 Y exit. The restored-exit tariff does not apply.

## Workflow feedback (optional)

The handoff named the 224-against-64 comparison directly, which made the check a width census on the pinned word. A link to discussion #1200 is enough; no separate session report.
